decisions.statement: The notes are part of Alan rather than a description of Alan.
The notes have no queue of subjects to work through.
A loose end is a finding.
A change here lands without Alan's review.

definition: the notes on who Alan is

description: This is the orientation an `/abby` interviewer loads before the first question. Its job is narrow and specific: surface the **unusual, easy-to-miss things** about Alan — the places where a normal-person prior would mislead you — so you don't open cold and don't spend the session re-deriving the architecture.

directives.name: Authorship
directives.act: Never write a claim about Alan he has not made.
directives.warrant: An invented sentence looks like one he said, so it reads as fact and nobody checks it again.
aids: Write what he said, never what it implies.
Mark your own reading and you may write it.

directives.name: Voice
directives.act: Write every note in Alan's first person.
directives.warrant: A third-person note has the same facts, so nothing but the voice shows it is not his.
aids: Convert every sentence, not just what he said.
Your own marked reading stays in your voice.
